title: Existence of thermodynamically consistent solutions for data-driven porous media problems
summary: Data-Driven Computational Mechanics (DDCM) replaces traditional phenomenological constitutive models by directly reformulating boundary-value problems in terms of local material state data obtained from experiments or fine-scale simulations. Standard DDCM formulations, only enforcing equilibrium and compatibility, do not inherently guarantee compliance with the second law of thermodynamics. This breakdown occurs particularly when input material data sets are subject to noise or local physical non-admissibility.
